summary: A dark figure at the windows turns, revealing himself as Morpheus, who greets Neo warmly and has him sit. Morpheus steers the conversation past flattery to why Neo is really there, naming the felt wrongness in the world and identifying it as the Matrix. He explains the Matrix as a mind-prison that blinds people from the truth, then admits no one can be told what it is — it must be seen. He offers two pills, blue to end the story and return to ignorance, red to learn the truth, and Neo swallows the red pill. Morpheus smiles and says 'Follow me.'

what_changes.before: A legend-seeker who knows something is wrong but cannot explain it, expecting the encounter to be unreal.
what_changes.after: Named the nature of his unease and shown that the choice before him is irreversible truth.
what_changes.evidence: You have the look of a man who accepts what he sees because he is expecting to wake up.

what_changes.before: Uncertain and physically anxious about the offer.
what_changes.after: Commits irrevocably by swallowing the red pill.
what_changes.evidence: Neo feels the smooth skin of the capsules, the moisture growing in his palms.

what_changes.before: A distant legend to be met.
what_changes.after: The guide offering truth and leading Neo onward.
what_changes.evidence: This is your last chance. After this, there is no going back.

event_hint.one_line: Morpheus tests and then recruits Neo, culminating in the choice of the red pill.

uncertain: What the truth behind the Matrix actually is.
Whether Trinity remains just outside the room after exiting.
The exact time of day, though thunder suggests stormy conditions.

minds.wants: To bring Neo to a genuine, self-authored choice to leave the Matrix — not to convince him, but to let him commit.
minds.feels: A controlled, patient certainty. He has done this before and knows the outcome can't be forced, only offered; underneath the ceremony is a man who has weighed this recruit against the risk and decided he is worth breaking a rule for.
minds.shows: Warmth and courtly ease — 'the honor is mine,' a smile that 'lights up the room,' unhurried hospitality — then a deliberate shift into surgical directness once he has Neo seated and settled.
minds.basis: He greets Neo warmly and deflects flattery ('I think we both know there's more to it than that'), reads Neo's face ('the look of a man who accepts what he sees because he is expecting to wake up'), refuses to explain the Matrix ('no one can be told... You have to see it'), and frames the pills as Neo's own irreversible decision ('all I am offering is the truth. Nothing more.').

believes_about.belief: That Neo is the one worth unplugging — that his lifelong 'splinter' and refusal of fate mark him as more than an ordinary recruit.
believes_about.wrong_because: The scene gives no confirmation that Neo is special; it only shows a frightened, curious man swallowing on damp palms. Morpheus's certainty about Neo's significance is a wager the story has not yet validated.

believes_about.belief: That Neo must choose freely rather than be told, because belief cannot be implanted by argument.
believes_about.wrong_because: He assumes the pill-choice is the honest test of will it appears to be, when in fact the red pill is a trace program that unmakes Neo's body regardless of how 'free' the choice feels — the freedom is real to Neo but the mechanism is far less voluntary than the ceremony implies.

minds.wants: To finally name and resolve the 'wrongness' he has felt his whole life — to stop being driven mad by a splinter he can't locate.
minds.feels: Awe tipping into dread. He expected this meeting to be unreal ('expecting to wake up'), and the dread comes when Morpheus confirms the feeling is real and that acting on it is irreversible; his moist palms and hard swallow are the body registering that this is not a game.
minds.shows: Nervous deference and a legend-fan's flattery ('It's an honor,' 'Most hackers would die to meet you'), then a quiet, committed nod and the physical act of swallowing — the only thing he lets be fully seen is the decision itself.
minds.basis: He echoes 'You could say that,' defends his need for control ('I don't like the idea that I'm not in control of my life'), names 'The Matrix?' as the thing he's felt, and, after Morpheus lays out the two irreversible paths, swallows the red pill while his palms sweat.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus is a legendary, all-knowing guide ('He knows more than you can possibly imagine,' per Trinity) whose offer is simply 'the truth, nothing more.'
believes_about.wrong_because: He doesn't yet know Morpheus is operating on a prophecy-driven agenda and a hidden motive for choosing him, nor that 'the truth' is not information but a physical unmaking — the awakening in the pod that follows.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus's warmth means he is safe and on Neo's side.
believes_about.wrong_because: The warmth is partly method — a deliberate technique to settle a recruit before testing and then leading him into an irreversible, dangerous act. Safety is not what Morpheus is offering; truth is, and they are not the same thing.

minds.wants: To deliver Neo to Morpheus intact and then remove herself so the recruitment can happen without her presence shaping it.
minds.feels: A disciplined restraint — she has brought him this far on faith, knows more than Neo does, but understands her role ends at the door and that the choice must be Neo's alone to make.
minds.shows: Near-silence and obedience: she says nothing here, only exchanges a nod with Morpheus and exits at his signal, leaving the two men to it.
minds.basis: She leads Neo to the room in sc-028 and advises 'Be honest. He knows more than you can possibly imagine,' then in this scene merely receives Morpheus's nod and 'exits through a door to an adjacent room,' taking no part in the exchange.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is worth the risk she has taken in bringing him to Morpheus.
believes_about.wrong_because: Nothing in this scene proves Neo will hold up; her confidence is a gamble on a man whose hands are shaking as he swallows, and the coming events will test whether her judgment was sound.

connects_back: Trinity's sc-028 counsel — 'Be honest. He knows more than you can possibly imagine' — is exactly how Neo behaves here, leading with confession and awe rather than posture.
Neo's whole-life 'something is wrong with the world' that Morpheus names is the itch that drove Neo's hacking and his search for Morpheus across the preceding scenes.
The storm/thunder and the decaying, liminal hotel setting carry the ominous register established as the car fled the wire tap (sc-026) and reached the deserted hotel (sc-027).
The recruitment is the payoff of the pursuit that Morpheus's crew has been running — the reason Neo was hunted, tested, and brought here at all.
sets_up: Neo's irreversible commitment, which makes the physical unplugging of ev-006 (the trace program activating and his digital body dissolving) both possible and unavoidable.
The awakening in the pod and transport out of the power plant (ev-007), since the red pill is what severs him from the Matrix rather than merely informing him.
The reconstruction on the Nebuchadnezzar (ev-008) and the historical/prophecy revelations (ev-009, ev-010), because Neo has now crossed the point of no return and cannot be put back.
Morpheus's role as guide ('Follow me'), establishing the teacher-recruit dynamic that governs Neo's orientation (ev-011) and combat training (ev-012).
dramatic_function: This scene is the threshold of the whole story: it converts Neo's vague, maddening unease into a named reality and then forces him to author his own irreversible crossing, transforming him from a seeker who expects to wake up into a man who has chosen not to — so that everything after is consequence, not possibility.
